items.class: E-06 register bleed carrying a byte-false cross-row claim (E-18 arm)
items.claim: The rival-defeating disclosure asserts that the natan-plus-lev construction 'opened the preceding row at 1:13'; 1:13 is that row's second verse, not its opening, and the assertion contradicts the neighbour row's own account of 1:13.
items.grounds: The preceding row's span Eccl.1.12-Eccl.1.15 opens at 1:12 with אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ (oshb:Eccl.1.12, byte tier); וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י stands at 1:13 (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier). The substantive recurrence the sentence exists to disclose is TRUE and survives the repair: וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier) and וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת (oshb:Eccl.1.17, byte tier) are both natan-root plus lev, so the row's 'disclosed here rather than implied absent' posture is honest and only the positional attribution is defective. Not load-bearing - the restart driver is the dibbarti verb (sweep: 2 verses, 1:16 and 2:15), which the row cites with its digit.
items.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: drop the positional row reference and the false 'opened' attribution, re-anchoring on the verse alone (e.g. 'the natan-plus-lev construction standing at 1:13 ... recurs inside this row at 1:17'). Span, refs, unit_type and confidence unaffected.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The preceding row's span is Eccl.1.12-Eccl.1.15 and its opening verse begins אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ (oshb:Eccl.1.12, byte tier; the verse's first four tokens); the natan-plus-lev construction וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier) stands in that row's SECOND verse, so the shipped clause 'the natan-plus-lev construction that opened the preceding row at 1:13' is false as a claim about the neighbour row, contradicts that row's own account (1:12 restates the royal self-identification; 1:13 'continues into the first wisdom inquiry'), and is a positional row reference the book's register purge bars outright. The recurrence the sentence exists to disclose is TRUE: וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת (oshb:Eccl.1.17, byte tier) is the same natan-root-plus-lev construction in a different inflected form (the 1:13 form recurs as a contiguous skeleton phrase at 2 verses book-wide, 1:13 and 8:16; the 1:17 form at 1 verse book-wide), so the 'disclosed here rather than implied absent' posture survives and the falsity is confined to the positional attribution. BOTH SIDES of the 1:15|1:16 seam weighed: 1:15 closes on the gnomic couplet וְחֶסְר֖וֹן לֹא יוּכַ֥ל לְהִמָּנֽוֹת (oshb:Eccl.1.15, byte tier) with no hevel refrain, and 1:16 opens on the self-address formula דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם לִבִּי֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.16, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses book-wide carry the dibbarti token, 1:16 and 2:15), the word-bound content-token intersection of 1:15 x 1:16 being empty; the formula onset decides the seam under the book's monologue rule, so the false clause is not load-bearing. Verdict: confirm at medium under the register lane's E-18 arm (a false cross-row claim, not load-bearing; low would understate a byte-false statement about a neighbour row's structure). Repair validated: re-anchoring on the verses alone ('the natan-plus-lev construction standing at 1:13 ... recurs inside this row at 1:17') is byte-sound provided 'recurs' is read as the same construction in different inflected forms rather than a word-bound identity; field repair only, no span effect.

items.class: rival-rejection warrant does not cross the contested seam
items.claim: The rival 'split the works catalogue from its wine-test introduction (2:3)' is rejected on cohesion evidence lying entirely inside 2:4-2:9, which says nothing about the contested 2:3|2:4 seam.
items.grounds: The row concedes the seam marker - 'MT 2:4 opens asyndetically ... a genuine clause break' - and then rejects the split 'on the lexical cohesion the ethical dative li and the mikol...lifnay...bi-Yerushalaim inclusio supply across web:Eccl.2.4-Eccl.2.9'. Re-derived from bytes, both cited objects stop short of the seam. Word-bound li per verse (skeleton token count, word-bound rather than substring, since a contiguous li sweep also returns amali-type tokens): 2:3 = 0, 2:4 = 2, 2:5 = 1, 2:6 = 1, 2:7 = 2, 2:8 = 2, 2:9 = 1, 2:10 = 0 - the run is real and unbroken over exactly 2:4-2:9 (6 verses, matching the row's digit) but does not touch 2:3 at all. The phrase inclusio is likewise confined to the same stretch (sweep lifnay-birushalaim: 2 verses, 2:7 and 2:9). Neither object bears on why 2:3 belongs with 2:4-2:10, so the warrant offered does not defeat the rival it is aimed at. Not alone load-bearing: the row's outer seams are independently warranted (tarti at 2:3, the turning formula at 2:11), and the embedded neighbour row supplies the cross-seam reading this rationale omits by treating 2:3 as the opening of one wine-building-accumulation experiment.
items.proposed_change: strongest_rejected_alternative / boundary_rationale field repair: replace the rejection ground with one that actually crosses 2:3|2:4 (e.g. the single first-person experiment frame opened at 2:3 whose self-benefit clauses 2:4-2:9 execute), or state plainly that the 2:3|2:4 clause break is conceded and the unit is held together on the experiment frame. No respan proposed - the span itself is not challenged.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The rival field concedes the clause break, הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י (oshb:Eccl.2.4, byte tier; the verse's asyndetic first tokens), and rejects the split on two objects that both stop short of the contested 2:3|2:4 seam: the word-bound skeleton token li counts 0 at 2:3, then 2/1/1/2/2/1 across 2:4-2:9 and 0 at 2:10 (six verses, matching the row's digit, none of them 2:3), and the contiguous skeleton phrase lifnay-birushalaim returns 2 verses book-wide (2:7, 2:9). The word-bound content-token intersection of 2:3 x 2:4 is EMPTY, so nothing the row cites explains why 2:3 belongs with 2:4-2:10; the warrant offered never reaches the rival it is aimed at. BOTH SIDES of the seam weighed under the book's monologue rule (formula onsets open units): 2:3 closes on its purpose clause מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּיהֶֽם (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) with no closural refrain, and 2:4 opens on a plain narrative perfect carrying no self-address or turning formula (the tarti frame תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) is unique, sweep: 1 verse book-wide; the turning formula u-faniti returns 2 verses, 2:11 and 2:12; no amarti, dibbarti, shavti or raiti token stands at 2:4), so no ruled onset device opens a unit at 2:4 and the rival fails on bytes the row never states. The outer seams are independently warranted (tarti at 2:3; the turning formula at 2:11), so the defect is a misdirected rival warrant, not load-bearing: confirm at medium. Repair validated with qualification: the experiment-frame ground is byte-sound (2:3's frame verb plus its purpose clause עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר אֶרְאֶ֗ה אֵי זֶ֨ה ט֜וֹב לִבְנֵ֤י הָאָדָם֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier), which the self-benefit catalogue of 2:4-2:9 executes) and may add the lexeme-level heart and wisdom bracket, וְלִבִּ֞י נֹהֵ֤ג בַּֽחָכְמָה֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) against כִּֽי לִבִּ֤י שָׂמֵ֨חַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.10, byte tier) and אַ֥ף חָכְמָתִ֖י עָ֥מְדָה לִּֽי (oshb:Eccl.2.9, byte tier), but only as root-level texture, never as word-bound identity (the 2:3 x 2:9 and 2:3 x 2:10 word-bound content intersections are also empty). Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative or boundary_rationale only; no respan.

items.class: seam warrant absent from the driver field / deferred to a boundary 'already established'
items.claim: The row states no affirmative byte warrant for either of its own seams: the opening seam is deferred to a boundary 'already established' by the preceding unit's shavti restart at 4:7, which warrants that unit's opening rather than the 4:8|4:9 seam, while two byte warrants standing at the seam itself go uncited.
items.grounds: boundary_rationale offers only continuity ('answers the solitary toiler of 4:8'), the unit's shape and its closing quotation; the only boundary-relevant byte evidence in the row - no first-person verb, the three-particle conditional run - sits in strongest_rejected_alternative as a unit_type argument, and device_notes then defers the seam to 'the independent shavti-restart boundary already established at web:Eccl.4.7-Eccl.4.8|Eccl.4.9'. The shavti restart stands in 4:7, i.e. it establishes the PRECEDING unit's opening (sweep shavti/veshavti: 3 verses - 4:1, 4:7, 9:11), and the preceding row as embedded likewise argues its own opening and 4:8's content but never its close. Two byte warrants at the seam are available and uncited: 4:8 closes on the verdict גַּם זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא (oshb:Eccl.4.8, byte tier), a closural refrain, and 4:9 opens on the comparative טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier) - a genuine tov-min construction with an intervening token, which is why it escapes the contiguous tov-min adjacency sweep and must be checked as a construction. Not alone load-bearing: the span itself is not challenged and the form evidence in the rival field is byte-true.
items.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: state the row's own seam warrant from the seam's own bytes (4:8's closural hevel verdict and 4:9's tov-min comparative opener) and move the form evidence out of the unit_type rival into the boundary case. No respan proposed.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The shavti turn stands at 4:7, וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי אֲנִ֛י וָאֶרְאֶ֥ה (oshb:Eccl.4.7, byte tier; sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry the shavti/veshavti token, 4:1, 4:7, 9:11), which establishes the PRECEDING unit's opening at 4:6|4:7, not the 4:8|4:9 seam this row's device_notes assigns to it ('the independent shavti-restart boundary already established at web:Eccl.4.7-Eccl.4.8|Eccl.4.9'); the embedded 4:7-4:8 row likewise argues its opening and 4:8's content but never its close, so the seam is un-argued from both rows. boundary_rationale names no seam device at all (continuity 'answers the solitary toiler of 4:8', the opening quotation, an illustration count and the closing quotation), and the only form evidence (no first-person verb; three distinct lead particles) sits in the unit_type rival. BOTH SIDES of 4:8|4:9 weighed from bytes: 4:8 closes on the verdict refrain גַּם זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא (oshb:Eccl.4.8, byte tier; the contiguous skeleton phrase gam-zeh-hevel returns 13 verses book-wide and the appended ve-inyan-ra 1 verse), a refrain close under the book's rule; 4:9 opens on the comparative טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier), a genuine tov-min construction whose plural first token and intervening subject keep it out of both the contiguous tov-min adjacency inventory and the tov-opener inventory (sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry the plural tovim, 4:9, 7:10, 11:6, only 4:9 verse-initial; the phrase min-ha-echad 1 verse); the word-bound content-token intersection of 4:8 x 4:9 is empty. Both sides decide the seam independently of the shavti restart, and the row's form claims re-derive true (no first-person -ti form and no ani token in 4:9-4:12; lead particles ki-im, gam-im, ve-im at their own refs). The rear seam also holds: 4:12 closes לֹ֥א בִמְהֵרָ֖ה יִנָּתֵֽק (oshb:Eccl.4.12, byte tier) and 4:13 opens on the inventory tov-opener ט֛וֹב יֶ֥לֶד מִסְכֵּ֖ן וְחָכָ֑ם (oshb:Eccl.4.13, byte tier), intersection empty. The span is unchallenged and the seam byte-sound, so the defect is an absent/misdirected warrant in the driver field: confirm at medium. Repair validated with qualification: restating the seam from 4:8's refrain close and 4:9's comparative onset is byte-sound, but 4:9 must be cited as a construction check with the digits above, not as an inventory site, and the cross-seam ordinal echo ve-ein-sheni (sweep: 2 verses, 4:8 and 4:10) stays disclosed as the row already does. Field repair only; no respan.

items.claim: The rival is characterised as the laughter ROOT with a book-wide digit of 2 verses, but that digit holds only for the defective spelling; the root stands in 5 verses book-wide across two attested spellings.
items.grounds: The row writes 'the laughter root, מִשְּׂחֹ֑ק (oshb:Eccl.7.3) / שְׂחֹ֣ק (oshb:Eccl.7.6) (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.7.3 and web:Eccl.7.6)'. A contiguous skeleton sweep of the defective spelling does return exactly those 2 verses, but the plene spelling with the mater vav escapes it: a skeleton sweep of the plene form returns 3 further verses -- MT 2:2 לִשְׂח֖וֹק, MT 3:4 לִשְׂח֔וֹק, MT 10:19 לִשְׂחוֹק֙ -- so the object the sentence NAMES occurs in 5 verses book-wide, not 2. This is the mater-lectionis hazard the book's own hazard catalog names (sweep per attested spelling; for a root-level claim sweep each spelling and say so) together with the count-object rule (name the object -- spelling vs root -- then count). It is not load-bearing: the rival is rejected on the token-empty MT 7:5 x MT 7:6 seam (re-derived: intersection empty) and on the mourning word's verified book-exclusivity, and the correction weakens the rival rather than the row, so no seam moves. check_universals.py does not catch it because the claim does carry a digit (11 claims seen, 0 flags).
items.proposed_change: Field repair only (no span effect): name the swept object as the spelling -- e.g. 'the defective laughter spelling (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.7.3 and web:Eccl.7.6; the plene spelling adds 3 further verses book-wide)' -- or restate the digit as the root's true 5-verse book-wide count.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes with the object named. The row attaches the digit to 'the laughter root' while quoting only the defective spelling: the contiguous skeleton sweep of that spelling returns 2 verses / 2 tokens book-wide, מִשְּׂחֹ֑ק (oshb:Eccl.7.3, byte tier) and שְׂחֹ֣ק (oshb:Eccl.7.6, byte tier); the plene spelling with the mater vav returns 3 further verses / 3 tokens, לִשְׂח֖וֹק (oshb:Eccl.2.2, byte tier), לִשְׂח֔וֹק (oshb:Eccl.3.4, byte tier) and לִשְׂחוֹק֙ (oshb:Eccl.10.19, byte tier); a token-level pass over all 222 MT verses finds no third spelling, so the root the sentence names stands in 5 verses / 5 tokens book-wide, not 2. This is the mater-lectionis hazard of the book's own catalogue (sweep per attested spelling; name spelling versus root before counting): a false digit for the named object. Not load-bearing, re-derived: the mourning word returns 2 verses book-wide (7:2, 7:4), both inside the span; the laughter-envelope rival is rejected on the word-bound content-token intersection of 7:5 x 7:6, which is EMPTY; and the corrected digit only weakens that rival, whose root is not exclusive to 7:3-7:6. BOTH SIDES of the 7:4|7:5 closing seam the envelope would erase: 7:4 closes וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִילִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית שִׂמְחָֽה (oshb:Eccl.7.4, byte tier) and 7:5 opens on the inventory tov-opener ט֕וֹב לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ גַּעֲרַ֣ת חָכָ֑ם (oshb:Eccl.7.5, byte tier; 4th of the chapter's 7 tov-opener sites), the formula onset deciding the seam, while the fools word straddling it (word-bound: 7:4, 7:5, 7:9) is disclosed by the row as topic texture. Confirm at medium. Repair validated: either wording proposed is byte-true (defective spelling 2 verses with the plene spelling adding 3 further verses, or the root at 5 verses book-wide); field repair only, no span effect.

items.claim: The row's first cross-seam disclosure quotes רָעָ֖ה as 'the raah root of oshb:Eccl.7.14's own closing imperative', but that run is the resh-ayin noun ('adversity'); the raah-root imperative in that verse is רְאֵ֑ה.
items.grounds: MT 7:14 carries both runs consecutively and both collate at BYTE tier at oshb:Eccl.7.14: רָעָ֖ה ('adversity', resh-ayin) followed immediately by the imperative רְאֵ֑ה ('consider', raah). device_notes item (1) attaches the raah-root label and the 'closing imperative' description to רָעָ֖ה; item (2) of the very same field then attaches רָעָ֖ה to the resh-ayin root ('two distinct objects on the same root, not blended') -- one byte run labelled two different roots inside one field. The neighbour row at web:Eccl.7.13-Eccl.7.14 argues the identical cross-seam tie with the correct token ('the raah root of its own closing imperative, רְאֵ֑ה'), so the two rows describe one seam with incompatible tokens. Byte-valid splice, semantically the wrong word for the claim. Not load-bearing: the seam itself stands on the perfect רָאִ֖יתִי (oshb:Eccl.7.15, byte tier) against the imperative register of 7:13-7:14, which the row also states.
items.proposed_change: device_notes item (1): replace the splice רָעָ֖ה with רְאֵ֑ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier). No dependent edit follows -- item (2) already carries רָעָ֖ה under the resh-ayin root, and the seam warrant is unchanged.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. oshb:Eccl.7.14 carries the two runs consecutively, רָעָ֖ה רְאֵ֑ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier): the first is the resh-ayin noun in וּבְי֥וֹם רָעָ֖ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier; the phrase is unique, sweep: 1 verse book-wide), the second the imperative רְאֵ֑ה גַּ֣ם אֶת זֶ֤ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier), the verse's last imperative after הֱיֵ֣ה בְט֔וֹב (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier) and matching the pair's opening imperative רְאֵ֖ה אֶת מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (oshb:Eccl.7.13, byte tier). device_notes item (1) labels the noun run as the raah root of 7:14's own closing imperative while item (2) of the same field correctly assigns that very run to the resh-ayin root: one byte run, two roots, one field. Byte-valid splice, semantically the wrong word for the claim, a defect regardless of when the ledger named the class. Ruled coherently with the neighbour row at Eccl.7.13-Eccl.7.14, which describes the same seam with the correct token (its closing imperative recurring as the perfect רָאִ֖יתִי (oshb:Eccl.7.15, byte tier)): the two rows must agree and the neighbour is right. BOTH SIDES of the 7:14|7:15 seam weighed: 7:14 closes on the purpose clause שֶׁלֹּ֨א יִמְצָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם אַחֲרָ֖יו מְאֽוּמָה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier) inside an imperative-register verse, and 7:15 opens on the observation frame אֶת הַכֹּ֥ל רָאִ֖יתִי בִּימֵ֣י הֶבְלִ֑י (oshb:Eccl.7.15, byte tier; the raiti token returns 18 verses book-wide and the inventory lists 7:15), the word-bound content-token intersection of 7:14 x 7:15 being empty; the register shift (imperative to first-person report) decides the seam, exactly as the row independently states, so the mis-splice is texture-level and not load-bearing. Confirm at medium. Repair validated: replacing the splice in item (1) with רְאֵ֑ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier) is byte-sound, with the one qualification that 'closing imperative' means the verse's last imperative, not its last word; item (2) already holds the noun under the resh-ayin root and needs no edit. Field repair only; no respan.

items.claim: The row twice states that web:Eccl.7.19 falls 'one verse outside' the sentence-literature zone's bound at web:Eccl.7.14; it falls five verses outside it.
items.grounds: The book's ruled sentence-literature zone in this chapter is 7:1-14, and ch 7 is identity (WEB 7:1-14 = MT 7:1-14), so no crosswalk question arises. web:Eccl.7.19 stands five verses past the zone's closing verse; the first verse outside the zone is web:Eccl.7.15, which the audited row at that verse itself treats as already reverted to the monologue register. The false distance is repeated in boundary_rationale ('though it falls one verse outside that zone's own bound at web:Eccl.7.14') and in device_notes ('single_saying is applied one verse outside this chapter's own designated sentence zone, which ends at web:Eccl.7.14'), and it is the proximity premise for the paired claim that the verse is 'of the same form as the sentence-zone sayings just before it' -- the sayings immediately before it (web:Eccl.7.16-Eccl.7.18) are the moderation admonition, not sentence-zone sayings, so that clause is unsupported once the distance is corrected. Not load-bearing on either seam (both rest on the register shifts named above); load-bearing on the unit_type deviation licence, which is what the row uses it for.
items.proposed_change: Correct the distance in both fields (web:Eccl.7.19 stands five verses past the zone's closing verse at web:Eccl.7.14), re-argue the single_saying deviation from the verse's own self-contained comparative construction alone rather than from proximity to the zone, and drop or re-anchor 'the same form as the sentence-zone sayings just before it'. unit_type, confidence and observed_substrate_signals re-open with the driver, per the dependent-field rule.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. Chapter 7 is identity (crosswalk: WEB 7:19 = MT 7:19, WEB 7:14 = MT 7:14), so web:Eccl.7.19 stands five verses past the ruled sentence zone's close at web:Eccl.7.14, the first verse outside it being web:Eccl.7.15; the row's twice-repeated 'one verse outside' (boundary_rationale and device_notes) is false. The proximity premise fails with it: the verses immediately before 7:19 are the moderation admonition of 7:16-7:18, closing on כִּֽי יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים יֵצֵ֥א אֶת כֻּלָּֽם (oshb:Eccl.7.18, byte tier), not sentence-zone sayings, and the row's own rival field and device_notes call the verse 'distinct in FORM' from the zone's tov-min sayings, contradicting boundary_rationale's 'of the same form as the sentence-zone sayings just before it' inside one row. BOTH SIDES of each seam weighed: 7:18's second-person prohibition series with its gnomic grounding clause closes against 7:19's third-person maxim onset הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תָּעֹ֣ז לֶחָכָ֑ם (oshb:Eccl.7.19, byte tier; the verb and the noun of its comparative מֵֽעֲשָׂרָה֙ שַׁלִּיטִ֔ים (oshb:Eccl.7.19, byte tier) each return 1 verse book-wide), and 7:19 closes אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ בָּעִֽיר (oshb:Eccl.7.19, byte tier) against 7:20's fresh maxim onset כִּ֣י אָדָ֔ם אֵ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק בָּאָ֑רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.7.20, byte tier); the word-bound content-token intersections 7:18 x 7:19 and 7:19 x 7:20 are both empty, so both seams rest on the register shifts the row states and neither moves. The false distance is not load-bearing on a seam, and not decisive for the unit_type licence either, since device_notes grounds the deviation on the verse's own construction (a verbal comparative with no observation frame), which re-derives true; it is a false positional digit deployed twice as a premise: confirm at medium. Repair validated with qualification: correct the distance in both fields, re-argue single_saying from the construction alone, and resolve the internal form contradiction in favour of the rival/device_notes reading (distinct in form, same genre), on which the licence actually depends; no driver swap is entailed, so unit_type and confidence re-open only formally and the bytes give no reason to change them. Field repair only; no respan.

items.claim: device_notes attaches the 20-verse ruach digit to 'the bare ruach word-bound form' and cites Eccl.11.5 as one of its two sites; the bare word-bound form stands at 13 verses book-wide, and Eccl.11.5 carries the definite form, not the bare one.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. items.claim: The splice-plus-gloss 'Job.9.23's NEQIYIM (mocks)' names the wrong word: the token glossed is the plural noun 'innocent ones', not the mocking verb the argument needs.
items.grounds: oshb:Job.9.23 reads (word order) ... לְמַסַּ֖ת / נְקִיִּ֣ם / יִלְעָֽג. The spliced token נְקִיִּ֣ם is the masculine plural of naqi, 'innocent (ones)', standing as the nomen rectum after the construct לְמַסַּ֖ת ('at the trial of'); WEB 9:23 renders it 'the innocent' ('If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.'). The subjectless 3ms verb the claim actually depends on is יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), the verse's final word. The syntactic observation ('no expressed subject of its own') is true of that verb and cannot be true of a noun in a construct chain, so the warrant survives with the right token; the cited token and gloss do not. Byte-valid splice, semantically wrong word for the claim.
items.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale swap the splice and gloss to the verse-final verb of oshb:Job.9.23, יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), re-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json; the surrounding sentence otherwise stands.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. oshb:Job.9.23 reads אִם שׁ֭וֹט יָמִ֣ית פִּתְאֹ֑ם לְמַסַּ֖ת נְקִיִּ֣ם יִלְעָֽג: word 5 לְמַסַּ֖ת is a construct noun ('at the trial of'), word 6 נְקִיִּ֣ם is the masculine plural of naqi, 'innocent (ones)', its nomen rectum, and word 7 יִלְעָֽג, the verse-final word, is the 3ms yiqtol 'he mocks'; WEB “If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.” web:Job.9.23. The shipped sentence splices נְקִיִּ֣ם and glosses it 'mocks' while arguing that it 'has no expressed subject of its own', a predication that is true of the verb יִלְעָֽג and impossible for a noun inside a construct chain. The splice is byte-valid (collates BYTE at oshb:Job.9.23) but names the wrong word for the claim: a wrong-token splice as filed. The underlying continuity observation survives with the right token (the explicit 3ms subject ה֣וּא of מְכַלֶּֽה at oshb:Job.9.22 carries over to the subjectless יִלְעָֽג), so the row's edges and band are untouched: not load-bearing (not high), and a semantically wrong quoted word is a defective warrant rather than a mechanical slip (not low): medium confirmed. Repair proposal validated: swapping the splice and gloss to the verse-final verb יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), re-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, matches the bytes; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only. both_sides_assessed false: the item concerns an intra-row token, not a seam.

items.claim: The row labels the chapter's 17-token particle series a 'protasis series' and draws its ordinals from that count, an object conflation the book's own ruling forbids and the adjacent row rejects.
items.grounds: Re-swept over verse_map_oshb.json (word-token search over the maqaf-free extract): the protasis particle stands in exactly 17 verses of Job 31 and is verse-initial in every one - Job.31.5, 31.7, 31.9, 31.13, 31.16, 31.19, 31.20, 31.21, 31.24, 31.25, 31.26, 31.29, 31.31, 31.33, 31.36, 31.38, 31.39. So '17', 'verse-initial' and the range Job.31.5 through Job.31.39 are TRUE, and Job.31.38 is the 16th and Job.31.39 the 17th TOKEN. But book LAW section 2e-b (ruling OL-c16) fixes the 17 as a PARTICLE-TOKEN count and excludes Job.31.36 אִם לֹ֣א עַל שִׁ֭כְמִי אֶשָּׂאֶ֑נּוּ (WEB: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, web:Job.31.36) as an oath affirmation rather than a protasis, stating that protasis-clause counts are a different object. At the protasis object the series has 16 members, and oshb:Job.31.38 אִם עָ֭לַי is the 15th while oshb:Job.31.39 אִם כֹּ֭חָהּ is the 16th - so 'the sixteenth' and 'the series' true seventeenth and closing member' are false under the label the row itself applies. The conflation also puts the row at odds with its own immediate predecessor: M8-Job-127 (span Job.31.35-Job.31.37) applies OL-c16 in its own prose, calling the Job.31.36 particle an oath-affirmation idiom answering the wish rather than opening a further self-curse. Not alone load-bearing: the opening seam rests on the verse-initial particle standing in oshb:Job.31.38's own bytes, byte-true independent of any ordinal.
items.proposed_change: Field repair only: name the object as the chapter's 17 verse-initial PARTICLE tokens (Job.31.5-Job.31.39) and either restate the ordinals at that object ('the sixteenth particle token') or give protasis-object ordinals with Job.31.36 excluded per LAW section 2e-b (Job.31.38 = 15th, Job.31.39 = 16th of 16). No span, seam or confidence change.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways (identity zone; runs spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, byte tier). Word-bound skeleton sweep of the particle אִם over Job 31 (maqaf-free extract): 17 tokens in 17 verses, every one verse-initial - Job.31.5, 31.7, 31.9, 31.13, 31.16, 31.19, 31.20, 31.21, 31.24, 31.25, 31.26, 31.29, 31.31, 31.33, 31.36, 31.38, 31.39 - so the row's '17-token', 'verse-initial skeleton sweep' and 'Job.31.5 through Job.31.39' are all true, oshb:Job.31.38 אִם עָ֭לַי אַדְמָתִ֣י תִזְעָ֑ק is the sixteenth token and oshb:Job.31.39 אִם כֹּ֭חָהּ אָכַ֣לְתִּי בְלִי כָ֑סֶף the seventeenth and last. Where the finding over-reads: the row does not draw its ordinals from a protasis-clause count. items.claim: The 'pit' recurrence sentence names the wrong Hebrew tokens: it cites 33:18's מֵעֲבֹ֥ר and 33:22's נַפְשׁ֑וֹ as the bare and prefixed pit forms, when the pit tokens are 33:18 שָׁ֑חַת (bare) and 33:22 לַשַּׁ֣חַת (prefixed).

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways (identity zone; runs spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, byte tier). oshb:Job.33.18 reads יַחְשֹׂ֣ךְ נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי שָׁ֑חַת וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ מֵעֲבֹ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁלַח (web:Job.33.18 “He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.”): the pit token is the fourth word שָׁ֑חַת, bare, while the token the row names as '33:18's bare' form is the sixth word מֵעֲבֹ֥ר, a mem-prefixed infinitive rendered 'from perishing' - neither bare nor 'pit'. oshb:Job.33.22 reads וַתִּקְרַ֣ב לַשַּׁ֣חַת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ לַֽמְמִתִֽים (web:Job.33.22 “Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.”): the pit token is the second word לַשַּׁ֣חַת, lamed-prefixed, while the token the row names as 33:22's 'prefixed form' is the third word נַפְשׁ֑וֹ, 'his soul', suffixed and unprefixed. adjudication.grounds: CONFIRM at medium; span ruling endorse_proposal, qualified below. Re-derived from bytes both ways. The seam: oshb:Prov.6.23 opens on the motive particle כִּ֤י נֵ֣ר and oshb:Prov.6.24 opens on the purpose infinitive לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת רָ֑ע (both byte tier), a lamed-infinitive with no finite clause of its own that hangs on what precedes - the row concedes this in its own rationale - and the seam carries neither ruled C1 signal: the chapter's word-bound vocative tokens stand at Prov.6.1 (word 1), Prov.6.3 (word 4) and Prov.6.20 (word 2, נְצֹ֣ר בְּ֭נִי, byte tier), none at Prov.6.24, and pmarks_Prov.json (WLC, single witness) carries PE at Prov.6.5, Prov.6.11, Prov.6.15, Prov.6.19, Prov.6.26 and Prov.6.35 - stated as inventory facts, never as absence-counterevidence. Exact skeleton-token overlap across Prov.6.23|Prov.6.24 is 0, so the seam rests on topic onset alone inside an argument that itself asserts syntactic continuity across it. Independent evidence the auditor did not cite settles the structure: the same purpose infinitive opens oshb:Prov.7.5, לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה (byte tier; word-bound sweep of the token לשמרך: 2 verses book-wide, Prov.6.24 and Prov.7.5, the two tokens byte-identical), and there it CLOSES the exordium (Prov.7.1 בְּ֭נִי שְׁמֹ֣ר אֲמָרָ֑י through Prov.7.5) before the narrative opens at oshb:Prov.7.6 with כִּ֭י בְּחַלּ֣וֹן בֵּיתִ֑י (byte tier); likewise oshb:Prov.5.2 לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מְזִמּ֑וֹת closes the Prov.5.1 vocative exordium before oshb:Prov.5.3 opens כִּ֤י נֹ֣פֶת (byte tier), and oshb:Prov.2.16 לְ֭הַצִּ֣ילְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה (byte tier) is the same purpose clause inside the chapter-length lecture. The book's own lecture template binds the keep-you-from-the-woman purpose clause to the preceding exordium, so the shipped Prov.6.23|Prov.6.24 seam cuts the template's own join; the rival's rejection is circular exactly as filed (the 6:26-corroborated split is refused on the strength of the 6:24 infinitive the row concedes depends on 6:23). Not high: nothing the row states is byte-false, the unit it draws has real internal glue (the woman-noun spine מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת רָ֑ע at oshb:Prov.6.24, וְאֵ֥שֶׁת אִ֑ישׁ at oshb:Prov.6.26, אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֵ֑הוּ at oshb:Prov.6.29, byte tier), and the placement is one of two defensible cuts, so the defect is a seam warrant, not a byte-false load-bearing claim. Both sides at the proposed seam Prov.6.26|Prov.6.27: oshb:Prov.6.26 is a complete motive clause, כִּ֤י בְעַד אִשָּׁ֥ה זוֹנָ֗ה through נֶ֖פֶשׁ יְקָרָ֣ה תָצֽוּד (byte tier), closing under the PE at Prov.6.26 (tier-3 weak, single witness, corroboration only); oshb:Prov.6.27 opens a new construction, the interrogative הֲיַחְתֶּ֤ה אִ֓ישׁ (byte tier), whose paired question at oshb:Prov.6.28 (אִם יְהַלֵּ֣ךְ אִ֭ישׁ) is answered by כֵּ֗ן הַ֭בָּא at oshb:Prov.6.29 (byte tier) - a self-contained question-question-application figure. One straddle must be disclosed by any replacement warrant: the exact skeleton token איש stands at word 9 of oshb:Prov.6.26 (וְאֵ֥שֶׁת אִ֑ישׁ) and word 2 of oshb:Prov.6.27 (אִ֓ישׁ), a high-frequency noun (word-bound sweep: 53 verses book-wide) that is 'another man' inside the wife-phrase at 6:26 and the generic subject of the questions at 6:27-28, a weak lexical straddle outweighed by the syntactic dependency the shipped seam cuts. Both sides at the erased seam: Prov.6.23 closes no unit by any ruled device (no vocative, no mark, no refrain; its close וְדֶ֥רֶךְ חַ֝יִּ֗ים תּוֹכְח֥וֹת מוּסָֽר completes the lamp metaphor and the dependent infinitive follows), so the proposal meets the both-sides law. Qualifications on the proposal: (1) the endorsed route is the seam relocation, giving M8-Prov-026 = Prov.6.20-Prov.6.26 (onset on the vocative at word 2 of Prov.6.20 under the PE closing Prov.6.19; close on the PE-corroborated motive clause) and M8-Prov-027 = Prov.6.27-Prov.6.29 - one edit, ruled coherently for both rows; (2) the merge alternative Prov.6.20-Prov.6.29 is not endorsed, since it would bury the one parashah-corroborated interior seam the C1 rule names; (3) the proposal's 'both units sit inside the ~4-8 verse C1 range' is wrong for Prov.6.27-Prov.6.29 (3 verses) - that unit stands on its own construction, not on length; (4) the rear seam Prov.6.29|Prov.6.30 (closing לֹ֥א יִ֝נָּקֶ֗ה at oshb:Prov.6.29; oshb:Prov.6.30 opening לֹא יָב֣וּזוּ לַ֭גַּנָּב, byte tier; overlap only the negative particle; no mark, no vocative) is untouched by the proposal and outside this ruling. Everything here remains a PROPOSAL for the owner remediation docket; nothing is adopted.

items.class: E-05 count-object discipline / incomplete set disclosure

With 8 verses carrying the root string and a same-construction sibling at Prov.10.6, 'the noun's rarity' is not supported by the cited 3, and the disclosure that names one omitted spelling set while omitting another reads as complete when it is not.

adjudication.grounds: CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived with the object named (sweep.py --skel, verse counts, plus word-bound token sweeps over verse_map_oshb.json): contiguous skeleton ברכה = 3 verses (Prov.10.7, Prov.11.25, Prov.11.26), the row's digit and set exactly; ברכת = 3 verses (Prov.10.22, Prov.11.11, Prov.24.25), the construct set the row discloses; ברכות = 2 verses (Prov.10.6, Prov.28.20), undisclosed; the root string ברכ = 8 verses, every hit a form of the same noun (per-verse tokens ברכות, לברכה, ברכת, בברכת, ברכה, וברכה, ברכת, ברכות; no verb or knee false hit, final-kaf allography excluded), so the auditor's digits are byte-true. The omitted set holds the nearest parallel to the row's own evidence: oshb:Prov.10.6 opens בְּ֭רָכוֹת לְרֹ֣אשׁ צַדִּ֑יק and oshb:Prov.11.26 closes וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ מַשְׁבִּֽיר (both byte tier), the same blessing-on-the-head construction with the byte-identical token לְרֹ֣אשׁ. A further byte fact strengthens the finding: at the lexeme level where 'the noun's rarity' is claimed, Prov.10.6|Prov.10.7 is a second ADJACENT pair of the noun (בְּ֭רָכוֹת at oshb:Prov.10.6 against לִבְרָכָ֑ה at oshb:Prov.10.7, byte tier), and that pair shares two exact skeleton tokens (צדיק, רשעים) where Prov.11.25|Prov.11.26 shares none (forms בְּרָכָ֥ה and וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה, byte tier, unequal at every tier), so the row's 'this pair alone stands adjacent among them' is true only for the 3-verse spelling object it names and would be false for the noun. Why medium and not high: the rarity leg is unquantified rather than byte-false (8 verses of 915 is genuinely infrequent), the exclusivity claim is object-scoped and true at its named object, and the cluster's edges do not rest on it - exact-token overlap Prov.11.24|Prov.11.25 = 0 and Prov.11.26|Prov.11.27 = 0, neither neighbor carries any form of the noun, and pmarks_Prov.json records no mark, paseq or K/Q in Prov.11.24-Prov.11.27. Both sides weighed: front seam Prov.11.24|Prov.11.25 - oshb:Prov.11.24 closes its existential saying on וְחוֹשֵׂ֥ךְ מִ֝יֹּ֗שֶׁר אַךְ לְמַחְסֽוֹר and oshb:Prov.11.25 opens נֶֽפֶשׁ בְּרָכָ֥ה (byte tier), a new subject, coherently with the preceding row, which refuses extension on the same noun ground (byte-true); rear seam Prov.11.26|Prov.11.27 - oshb:Prov.11.26 closes on וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ מַשְׁבִּֽיר and oshb:Prov.11.27 opens שֹׁ֣חֵֽר ט֭וֹב (byte tier), a new seek/find subject, coherently with the following row. Under the C2 single-proverb default the cluster stands on a lexeme-level catchword (0 exact tokens) plus the giving/withholding pattern, the sub-two-token class the strategy expects at low confidence, so medium_low with the frontier flag is calibrated and the lowband disposition stands. Repair validated: the proposal's digits are byte-true; add to it that the 'alone adjacent' claim must be restated as spelling-scoped, or extended to disclose the Prov.10.6|Prov.10.7 adjacent pair, before the rarity leg can stand.

items.claim: The cluster's sole cohesion warrant — an 'exact same noun ... byte tier' repetition, restated in observed_substrate_signals as an 'exact skeleton token ... repeated' — is byte-false at both tiers it names, leaving the C2 atomic default live.

adjudication.grounds: DOWNGRADE high to medium; span ruling decline_proposal for the split, with the restatement route endorsed as the repair. Re-derived from bytes: the two forms are וּלְשׁ֖וֹן (oshb:Prov.12.18, word 5 of 7) and לְשׁ֣וֹן (oshb:Prov.12.19, word 7 of 8), byte tier, unequal at byte, NFD, accent_stripped and skeleton tiers (skeletons ולשון against לשון, the conjunction prefix breaking the identity); exact skeleton-token overlap Prov.12.18|Prov.12.19 = 0; word-bound token ולשון = 3 verses (Prov.10.31, Prov.12.18, Prov.25.15), word-bound token לשון = 12 verses, contiguous substring לשון = 16 verses - three different objects, none named by the row. So the auditor is right that 'the exact same noun ... byte tier', 'exact skeleton token ... repeated' and 'one content token' are false at the token tier they name, and that the waw prefix is nowhere disclosed. Why not high: the fact the warrant rests on - the noun for tongue standing in both adjacent verses - is byte-true at lexeme tier (both quoted forms are exact byte splices at their refs and visibly differ by the prefix), and the book's cluster bar does not require exact shared tokens: the strategy admits proverb_cluster on byte-grounded cohesion evidence named in the rationale (a catchword chain among the named classes) and places catchword clusters thinner than two shared content tokens in the expected-low-confidence class, while the exact-token adjacency figure is a staged texture signal, never row evidence; the corpus's own sibling at Prov.11.25-Prov.11.26 ships on exactly this class (בְּרָכָ֥ה against וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה, byte tier, 0 exact tokens) with the prefix disclosed, at medium_low. The lowband trigger resolves the same way: medium_low with the frontier flag is the calibrated band for a one-lexeme catchword, and the row's comparison class is imprecise rather than false - Prov.13.19|Prov.13.20 shares the exact skeleton token כסילים (כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים at oshb:Prov.13.19 against כְסִילִ֣ים at oshb:Prov.13.20, byte tier, accents differ), this row shares a lexeme only. Both sides weighed under the C2 default: front seam Prov.12.17|Prov.12.18 - oshb:Prov.12.17 closes on וְעֵ֖ד שְׁקָרִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה and oshb:Prov.12.18 opens יֵ֣שׁ בּ֭וֹטֶה (byte tier), overlap 0, coherently with the preceding row's no-shared-lexeme rejection (byte-true); rear seam Prov.12.19|Prov.12.20 - oshb:Prov.12.19 closes on לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר and oshb:Prov.12.20 opens מִ֭רְמָה בְּלֶב (byte tier), overlap 0, coherently with the following row. Texture noted, not ruled: a non-adjacent deceit web spans Prov.12.17-Prov.12.20 (שְׁקָרִ֣ים at oshb:Prov.12.17 against שָֽׁקֶר at oshb:Prov.12.19, root-level; מִרְמָֽה at oshb:Prov.12.17 against מִ֭רְמָה at oshb:Prov.12.20, the same skeleton token), straddling neither seam; the row discloses the falsehood-root part of it. pmarks_Prov.json: no mark, paseq or K/Q at Prov.12.17-Prov.12.20. Span ruling: the split into Prov.12.18-Prov.12.18 and Prov.12.19-Prov.12.19 is declined because its sole premise - that the bar demands exact shared tokens - is not the book's rule; the field repair is the sound route: restate at lexeme tier, disclose the waw-prefixed form at Prov.12.18 against the bare form at Prov.12.19, and name the three digits and objects above; observed_substrate_signals, strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence re-open with it. A PROPOSAL only; should the owner instead rule the cluster bar to exact shared tokens, the split follows and this ruling is conditional on that bar.

items.claim: The cluster's forward seam carries an undisclosed straddling catchword exactly as heavy as the row's own internal glue, and the row nonetheless ships at medium with no frontier posture, against the book's own sub-two-token rule.
items.grounds: Skeleton content-token overlap computed from consonantal_index.json. Prov.14.12 and Prov.14.13 share exactly ONE token (וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ, byte at oshb:Prov.14.13; the 14:12 form וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ is byte at oshb:Prov.14.12) and that single token is the row's entire lexical glue. adjudication.grounds: CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived from bytes (exact skeleton tokens from verse_map_oshb.json word splits): Prov.14.12|Prov.14.13 share one token, וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ (oshb:Prov.14.12, word 6) and וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ (oshb:Prov.14.13, word 5), byte tier, unequal at byte (accents differ) and equal at accent_stripped and skeleton tiers - the row's 'byte tier' is a splice-accuracy label, not an identity claim, and the identity holds one tier down; that token is the row's whole lexical glue. Prov.14.13|Prov.14.14 ALSO share exactly one token, and it is stronger on the bytes: לֵ֑ב (oshb:Prov.14.13, word 4) and לֵ֑ב (oshb:Prov.14.14, word 4) are byte-IDENTICAL, both carrying the atnach, i.e. both A-colon-final - slot-parallel in the same way the row's hinge word is B-colon-initial in both its verses. Neither this row nor the Prov.14.14 row discloses it, so the standing cross-seam rule (a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed) is breached at the row's forward edge. The backward seam Prov.14.11|Prov.14.12 carries a root-level straddle only, יְשָׁרִ֣ים (oshb:Prov.14.11) against יָ֭שָׁר (oshb:Prov.14.12), byte tier, 0 exact tokens; Prov.14.14|Prov.14.15 shares 0. Also byte-checked: oshb:Prov.14.12 and oshb:Prov.16.25 are byte-identical whole verses (the row's verbatim claim is true at the tier it names; the full-line skeleton sweep returns 2 verses, and the hinge-word sweep ואחריתה returns 5 verses, Prov.5.4, Prov.14.12, Prov.14.13, Prov.16.25, Prov.20.21, of which only Prov.14.12 and Prov.14.13 are adjacent - the missing digits behind the excl trigger, low). Severity medium, not high: the seam remains distinguishable, because the row's second ground is real - the appearance-versus-outcome template pivots on the shared hinge in both Prov.14.12 and Prov.14.13 and is absent from Prov.14.14 (no ואחריתה token there) - so the cluster is under-warranted at its edge rather than byte-false; and not low, because an undisclosed straddle of equal-or-greater weight at the very seam is a warrant defect, not a register one. Both sides weighed: the row opens on יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר (oshb:Prov.14.12, byte tier), a new existential subject after the house/tent antithesis closing oshb:Prov.14.11 (וְאֹ֖הֶל יְשָׁרִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיחַ, byte tier); it closes on וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ שִׂמְחָ֣ה תוּגָֽה (oshb:Prov.14.13, byte tier) while oshb:Prov.14.14 opens מִדְּרָכָ֣יו יִ֭שְׂבַּע ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב (byte tier), a new subject that nevertheless ends its A-colon on the same byte-identical token as the row's own last A-colon. pmarks_Prov.json: no mark, paseq or K/Q in Prov.14.11-Prov.14.15. Ruled coherently with M8-Prov-159#1 on the shared Prov.14.13|Prov.14.14 seam: the straddle is undisclosed on both sides, the cure is one seam-pair disclosure edit shared by both rows, and neither row's placement changes. Repair validated: disclose and weigh the straddle; the confidence re-band to medium_low with the frontier posture is endorsed as a proposal, since under the strategy's own wording a one-token catchword cluster is the sub-two-token class, the template being a construction-level ground rather than a second content token; the alternative route (adding a second byte-grounded shared content token) is not available from the bytes, since the two verses share no second exact token.

items.claim: The disclaimer that the verse 'shares no lexeme' with Prov.13.1-13.2 is byte-false: it shares two lexemes with Prov.13.2.
items.grounds: boundary_rationale asserts the verse 'is not adjacent to those and shares no lexeme with them'. Skeleton content-token comparison from consonantal_index.json: Prov.14.14 and Prov.13.2 share TWO tokens. oshb:Prov.13.2 carries אִ֭ישׁ and ט֑וֹב; oshb:Prov.14.14 carries אִ֣ישׁ and טֽוֹב - the same two lexemes, differing only in accents. It is a no-class universal shipped without a digit, and check_universals does not carry this phrasing in its lexicon, so it passed Tier-0 unflagged. It is not load-bearing - the boundary rests on the in-verse ellipsis and the rejected alternative rests on the compound noun's gloss being unnecessary - hence medium, not high.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: strike the disclaimer, or correct it to name the two shared lexemes and state that the shared vocabulary is generic and non-adjacent, so the comparison is not a cohesion claim.

adjudication.grounds: CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived from bytes: oshb:Prov.14.14 shares two exact skeleton tokens with oshb:Prov.13.2 - אִ֭ישׁ and ט֑וֹב at Prov.13.2 against אִ֣ישׁ and טֽוֹב at Prov.14.14 (byte tier; accents differ, skeletons איש and טוב equal) - and none with oshb:Prov.13.1, so 'shares no lexeme with them' is byte-false for one of the two verses it names. Object and digit for the register the claim lives in: word-bound איש = 53 verses and word-bound טוב = 52 verses book-wide, so the shared vocabulary is generic, which is exactly why the false disclaimer carries no cohesion weight - the row offers it to deny a tie with non-adjacent verses. Severity medium, not high or low: a false claim is a defect regardless of its argumentative weight, but the seam does not rest on it - the boundary rests on the in-verse ellipsis (the B-colon וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב carries no verb; the A-colon verb יִ֭שְׂבַּע is supplied), the rival rests on the crux noun's gloss being unnecessary, and the C2 atomic default governs. Both sides weighed: front seam Prov.14.13|Prov.14.14 - oshb:Prov.14.13 closes on וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ שִׂמְחָ֣ה תוּגָֽה and this verse opens מִדְּרָכָ֣יו יִ֭שְׂבַּע ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב (byte tier), a new subject, but its A-colon ends on the byte-identical token לֵ֑ב that ends the A-colon of oshb:Prov.14.13 (לֵ֑ב), an undisclosed straddle ruled coherently with M8-Prov-158#1: one seam-pair disclosure edit shared by both rows, no change of placement on either side; rear seam Prov.14.14|Prov.14.15 - this verse closes on וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב and oshb:Prov.14.15 opens פֶּ֭תִי יַאֲמִ֣ין (byte tier), 0 shared tokens, coherently with the following row's separate-vocabulary rejection. pmarks_Prov.json: no mark, paseq or K/Q at Prov.14.13-Prov.14.15; medium_low with the frontier flag is calibrated for the crux, so the lowband disposition stands. Repair validated: strike the disclaimer, or restate it as sharing only the generic tokens for man and good with Prov.13.2 and nothing with Prov.13.1, which is what the bytes support.

items.claim: The cluster's designated load-bearing warrant - an a-fortiori dependency running from 19:6 into the opening of 19:7 - is byte-false; the a-fortiori operates inside 19:7.
items.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative: 'the particle opening 19:7 grammatically depends on the claim just made in 19:6'; device_notes: 'the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between 19:6 and 19:7'. Residual cross-seam glue is root-level only (הָ֝רֵ֗עַ against מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ), and the exact form at 19:7 recurs at the non-adjacent 19:4, disclosed by the row.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL (routes onward, not applied): retire the Prov.19.6-Prov.19.7 proverb_cluster and re-cut as two single_proverb rows, Prov.19.6-Prov.19.6 and Prov.19.7-Prov.19.7, per the C2 atomic default, disclosing the shared friend-root at 19:4/19:6/19:7 as texture in each. If the cluster is instead retained, the replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original: no discourse-dependency claim across the 19:6|19:7 seam, root-level glue only, band dropped to low, with observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and strongest_rejected_alternative re-opened as dependent fields.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, every Hebrew run spliced from verse_map_oshb.json at byte tier. oshb:Prov.19.7 opens כָּ֥ל (0-based token 0 of 14, counting the inline ketiv), a quantifier, not a particle; the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י stands at 0-based tokens 4-5, and the atnach (U+0591) sits on מִמֶּ֑נּוּ, so the pair governs the move from כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי רָ֨שׁ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ ('all the brothers of a poor man hate him') to אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ ('how much more do his companions keep far from him'), web:Prov.19.7 “how much more do his friends avoid him!” - the intensified term is the companions, INSIDE 19:7. The row's 'the particle opening 19:7 grammatically depends on the claim just made in 19:6' and its 'how much more do even kin flee the poor' are therefore both byte-false: no particle opens the verse, and kin are the base case of the a-fortiori, not its intensified term. items.grounds: oshb:Prov.25.10 opens with פֶּֽן, a subordinating particle, and contains no governing clause; its governing prohibition אַל תְּגָֽל stands in oshb:Prov.25.9. This is not a punctuation argument: the particle is in the MT bytes. Book-wide byte control: exactly 7 Prov verses open with pen (Prov.5.9, Prov.5.10, Prov.22.25, Prov.24.18, Prov.25.10, Prov.30.9, Prov.31.5; sweep: 7 verses), and in all 7 the governing clause stands in the PREVIOUS verse, while the pen clauses of oshb:Prov.25.8, oshb:Prov.25.16 and oshb:Prov.25.17 all sit inside their own verse. The row's warrant, that the verse 'introduces its own subject and predicate', is true of the clause internally, יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ (oshb:Prov.25.10), but does not make a pen clause an independent unit. The owner S6 ruled precedent B-10, that a syntactically continuous single sentence spanning two verses is ONE proverb-unit typed single_proverb regardless of verse count, is directly on point. On file as the counter-argument: the 25:9 row reads the dependency as 'a warning appended after an already-complete instruction rather than a syntactic requirement for v9 to parse', which tests v9's parsability, not whether v10 can stand as a unit.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL for adjudication: merge into one single_proverb row spanning Prov.25.9-Prov.25.10, respanning the 25:9 row to Prov.25.9-Prov.25.10 and retiring this row, with the pen subordination named as the byte warrant and the B-10 precedent cited. Dependent fields to re-open on the swap: observed_substrate_signals, unit_type, strongest_rejected_alternative, confidence.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived (byte tier): oshb:Prov.25.10 reads פֶּֽן יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ וְ֝דִבָּתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תָשֽׁוּב and opens with the subordinator פֶּֽן; it contains no governing clause, and the prohibition it depends on, וְס֖וֹד אַחֵ֣ר אַל תְּגָֽל, closes oshb:Prov.25.9. Book-wide byte control (skeleton tier, first token): exactly 7 Prov verses open with פן (Prov.5.9, 5.10, 22.25, 24.18, 25.10, 30.9, 31.5), and in all 7 the governing clause stands in the previous verse - וְאַל תִּ֝קְרַ֗ב (5:8) before 5:9-10, אַל תִּ֭תְרַע (22:24) before 22:25, אַל תִּשְׂמָ֑ח and אַל יָגֵ֥ל (24:17) before 24:18, אַל תְּגָֽל (25:9) before 25:10, אַל תִּֽתֶּן לִ֑י (30:8) before 30:9, אַ֣ל לַֽמְלָכִ֣ים שְׁתוֹ יָ֑יִן (31:4) before 31:5 - while every other occurrence in Prov.25 (פֶּ֣ן at 25:8, פֶּן at 25:16, פֶּן at 25:17) sits inside its own verse after its own command; word-bound פן: 17 verses book-wide. A verse-initial פן is therefore, without exception in this book, the continuation of the preceding verse's sentence. The row's warrant ('introduces its own subject and predicate') is true of the clause's internal syntax, יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ, and irrelevant to its dependency; its other ground (25:9/25:10 share 0 exact skeleton tokens) re-derives true and is equally irrelevant, since a subordinate clause needs no catchword. The owner precedent B-10 (a syntactically continuous single sentence spanning two verses is ONE proverb-unit regardless of verse count, ruled at Prov.26.18-19) is directly on point; the 25:9 row's contrast ('the true syntactic split at 26:18-19') fails, because 26:18 כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ / 26:19 כֵּֽן (simile protasis and apodosis) and 25:9 / 25:10 (prohibition and its dependent clause) are the same class of cross-verse syntactic continuity, and its test ('a syntactic requirement for v9 to parse') asks whether 25:9 can stand, not whether 25:10 can. Load-bearing boundary defect: high confirmed. BOTH SIDES of the 25:9|25:10 seam: 25:9 closes וְס֖וֹד אַחֵ֣ר אַל תְּגָֽל - a vetitive is a governing onset device in the strategy's admonition shape, never a ruled close, and here demonstrably no close because the next verse opens with its dependent clause; 25:10 opens פֶּֽן יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ, web:Prov.25.10 “lest one who hears it put you to shame”, with no onset device (no header, vocative, formula or shared token); the governing rule is syntactic continuity (B-10). Rear edge of the merged unit: 25:10 closes וְ֝דִבָּתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תָשֽׁוּב and 25:11 opens תַּפּוּחֵ֣י זָ֭הָב, 0 shared skeleton tokens and a new image, so the seam against row Prov.25.11-Prov.25.12 holds. Front edge: the 25:8|25:9 seam is adjudicated at item M8-Prov-430#1 and ruled coherently with this one (25:8 stays a single row under that item's no-respan proposal; the 25:9|25:10 join is compelled, the 25:8|25:9 join optional). SPAN RULING endorse_proposal: merge into one row Prov.25.9-Prov.25.10, retiring Prov.25.10-Prov.25.10, with the verse-initial פן named as the byte warrant - a PROPOSAL for the owner docket, nothing applied. Qualification on the replacement claims: the proposal's unit_type single_proverb (per B-10) is not settled by B-10 alone, because 25:9 carries a governing imperative רִ֣יב plus the vetitive אַל תְּגָֽל and 25:10 is their motive clause, the command-plus-motive shape the owner precedent B-8 types admonition_unit even inside sentence collections (with a one-sentence deviation disclosure in C5); unit_type, observed_substrate_signals, strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence are dependent fields re-opened by the swap, as the proposal states.

items.grounds: The row states 'No merge with 25:15 or 25:17 was warranted; both are topically unrelated and share no skeleton token with this verse.' The 25:15 half is true (25:15 to 25:16 shows 0 shared exact skeleton tokens). The 25:17 half is false: 25:16 and 25:17 share the exact skeleton token pen, byte-identical in both verses, פֶּן (oshb:Prov.25.16) and פֶּן (oshb:Prov.25.17). Beyond the token they share the sin-bet-ayin root in the same slot, תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ (oshb:Prov.25.16) against יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ (oshb:Prov.25.17), and the pen-plus-suffixed-yiqtol construction built on that root stands at exactly 4 verses book-wide (Prov.5.10, Prov.25.16, Prov.25.17, Prov.30.9; sweep: 4 verses), of which oshb:Prov.25.16 and oshb:Prov.25.17 are the ONLY adjacent pair. Both verses are admonitions against having too much of a thing. Nothing of this straddling device is disclosed here, while the 25:17 row does disclose the sin-bet-ayin root at the same seam. Load-bearing: this sentence is the entire stated warrant for rejecting the strongest rival, and a shared construction run is one of the owner gate's named cluster warrants for C5; the same run clusters oshb:Prov.25.11-Prov.25.12 on 1 shared content token plus adjacency, a thinner case than this one. Confidence high is correspondingly over-stated.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The shipped rival ground 'share no skeleton token with this verse' is true for 25:15 and byte-false for 25:17: the word-bound skeleton-token intersection oshb:Prov.25.15|oshb:Prov.25.16 is 0 tokens, oshb:Prov.25.16|oshb:Prov.25.17 is 1 token, the lest-particle, byte-identical at the byte tier as פֶּן (oshb:Prov.25.16) and פֶּן (oshb:Prov.25.17). The auditor's root and construction claims hold with one count-object correction: the sin-dotted satisfied-sense root (skeleton שבע, sin-dotted forms only; the shin-dotted seven/swear homograph is a separate 6-verse object) stands in 19 verses book-wide (sweep, verses), here as תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ (oshb:Prov.25.16) and יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ (oshb:Prov.25.17), both byte tier; the lest-particle immediately followed by a yiqtol of that root stands in exactly 4 verses (sweep, verses: Prov.5.10, Prov.25.16, Prov.25.17, Prov.30.9), but the auditor's label 'pen-plus-suffixed-yiqtol' fits only 2 of the 4, because פֶּֽן יִשְׂבְּע֣וּ (oshb:Prov.5.10) is an unsuffixed plural and פֶּ֥ן אֶשְׂבַּ֨ע (oshb:Prov.30.9) an unsuffixed first person, so the object-suffixed form of the construction is confined to this seam's two verses, which are also the only adjacent pair of the 4; the correction narrows the object and strengthens the finding. The whole frame is shared: imperative אֱכֹ֣ל (oshb:Prov.25.16) / הֹקַ֣ר (oshb:Prov.25.17), then the lest-particle plus the suffixed yiqtol, then a suffixed consequence verb וַהֲקֵֽאתֽוֹ (oshb:Prov.25.16) / וּשְׂנֵאֶֽךָ (oshb:Prov.25.17), all byte tier. BOTH SIDES of the seam the rival concerns, 25:16|25:17: the closing verse דְּבַ֣שׁ מָ֭צָאתָ אֱכֹ֣ל דַּיֶּ֑ךָּ פֶּן תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ וַהֲקֵֽאתֽוֹ (oshb:Prov.25.16) and the opening verse הֹקַ֣ר רַ֭גְלְךָ מִבֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֑ךָ פֶּן יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ וּשְׂנֵאֶֽךָ (oshb:Prov.25.17), both byte tier; under the book's governing rule (C5 single-proverb default; a cluster only on named byte-grounded cohesion such as a pair grouping or a shared construction run) the shared construction is exactly a named warrant class, while each verse remains a syntactically complete admonition opened by its own imperative, so the rule permits the pair and does not compel it. The outer seams of the proposed pair are clean at both edges: oshb:Prov.25.15|oshb:Prov.25.16 shares 0 tokens (25:15 closes on the observation בְּאֹ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם יְפֻתֶּ֣ה קָצִ֑ין וְלָשׁ֥וֹן רַ֝כָּ֗ה תִּשְׁבָּר גָּֽרֶם (oshb:Prov.25.15), byte tier) and oshb:Prov.25.17|oshb:Prov.25.18 shares 0 tokens (25:18 opens a new simile, מֵפִ֣יץ וְ֭חֶרֶב וְחֵ֣ץ שָׁנ֑וּן אִ֥ישׁ עֹנֶ֥ה בְ֝רֵעֵ֗הוּ עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר (oshb:Prov.25.18), byte tier; the neighbour-word echo רֵעֶ֑ךָ (oshb:Prov.25.17) / בְ֝רֵעֵ֗הוּ (oshb:Prov.25.18) is root-level only, no shared token, and carries none of the construction). The auditor's comparison to the shipped pair Prov.25.11-Prov.25.12 is byte-true: oshb:Prov.25.11|oshb:Prov.25.12 shares 2 tokens, זָ֭הָב (oshb:Prov.25.11) / זָ֭הָב (oshb:Prov.25.12) byte-identical plus the particle על (skeleton-tier mention), i.e. 1 content token plus adjacency, thinner than this seam's token plus root plus construction. Severity: the false sentence is the entire stated warrant for rejecting the strongest rival, the straddling device is undisclosed in every field of the row, and confidence high rests on it, so the defect is load-bearing and high is confirmed. Adjacent-row coherence: the 25:17 row (M8-Prov-438) discloses only the root at its broad 19-verse object and calls it too frequent to bound a unit, which is true of the root and silent on the shared lest-particle token and the 2-verse suffixed construction; whichever arm is adopted must be applied to that row coherently (retired under arm b, or its disclosure completed under arm a). Span ruling endorse_proposal: the respan Prov.25.16-Prov.25.17 as one proverb_cluster is byte-sound under the owner gate's own construction-run warrant and rests on more than the shipped 25:4-5 and 25:11-12 pairs; arm a (atomic rows retained, dead warrant replaced, device disclosed) is also byte-compliant because the default is atomic and each verse is complete, so the choice between the arms is owner triage, and a replacement warrant under arm a passes the test that killed the original only if it names the shared lest-particle token, the suffixed-yiqtol construction and its 2-verse book-wide count and argues the atomic default over them. Nothing is adopted here; both arms remain proposals for the owner docket.

items.class: E-18 lost corpus-wide order + count-object discipline
items.claim: The ketiv/qere recurrence is counted inside a writer part and the digit 3 does not belong to the object the row names: that pair stands in 6 verses book-wide.
items.grounds: The row's own site is byte-true: oshb:Prov.27.15 carries the inline unpointed ketiv מדונים before the pointed qere מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים (both collate byte at Prov.27.15; pmarks_Prov.json kq records 1 note there, single witness). But 'in this part' scopes the recurrence count to the writer part, and the digit 3 does not belong to the object the row names. sweep.py --skel returns the ketiv skeleton in 6 verses book-wide (18:19, 21:19, 23:29, 25:24, 26:21, 27:15) and pmarks_Prov.json records a kq note at every one of them, so the ketiv/qere pair recurs at 6 verses, not 3; the pointed qere simply differs at three of them (מִדְיָנִ֣ים at oshb:Prov.21.19, מִדְיָנִ֨ים at oshb:Prov.23.29, and the waw-prefixed pair ומדונים וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים at oshb:Prov.18.19). The digit 3 is reproducible only at an unnamed accent-identical tier, where the run מדונים מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים is byte-identical at oshb:Prov.25.24, oshb:Prov.26.21 and oshb:Prov.27.15. Scoping the count to a writer part makes 3 come out right by coincidence and hides half the corpus-wide motif the row calls 'a recurring motif'.
items.proposed_change: Field repair: name the swept object and its tier and give both digits, e.g. the ketiv/qere pair stands in 6 verses book-wide (18:19, 21:19, 23:29, 25:24, 26:21, 27:15), of which 3 carry the accent-identical run (25:24, 26:21, 27:15). Delete 'in this part' from boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative and observed_substrate_signals; if the three accent-identical sites are kept as texture, keep them at that tier, and if the 6-verse set is argued instead, mirror oshb:Prov.18.19, oshb:Prov.21.19 and oshb:Prov.23.29 into boundary_evidence_refs. No span or seam change: oshb:Prov.27.14 / oshb:Prov.27.15 and oshb:Prov.27.15 / oshb:Prov.27.16 share zero word-bound skeleton tokens, so both edges stand.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The row's own site is byte-true: the inline unpointed ketiv מדונים (oshb:Prov.27.15) precedes the pointed qere מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.27.15), both byte tier, and pmarks_Prov.json kq records 1 note at Prov.27.15 (single witness). The auditor's book-wide digits re-derive exactly: the ketiv skeleton מדונים (skeleton-tier mention) stands in 6 verses (sweep, contiguous skeleton substring, verses: Prov.18.19, Prov.21.19, Prov.23.29, Prov.25.24, Prov.26.21, Prov.27.15), as the bare token in 5 and waw-prefixed in 1 (ומדונים at oshb:Prov.18.19, byte tier), with a kq note at every one of the 6; the two-token ketiv-plus-qere run is byte-identical at exactly 3 sites, מדונים מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.25.24), מדונים מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.26.21) and מדונים מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.27.15), while the qere differs by accent only at מִדְיָנִ֣ים (oshb:Prov.21.19) and מִדְיָנִ֨ים (oshb:Prov.23.29) and by waw prefix plus accent at וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.18.19); at the skeleton tier the pair is identical at 5 verses, 6 with the prefixed form. The severity turns on whether the row states anything false, and it does not: 'the same pair attested at 25:24 and 26:21 in this part' and 'recurs at 3 non-adjacent verses in this part' are true at the skeleton tier within the writer part, because chapters 25-27 hold exactly those 3 of the 6 sites, and the row nowhere says only. What is defective is the scope and the tier: 'in this part' is workflow register (a writer-part range) that hides the corpus-wide order of a motif the row itself calls recurring, and the unnamed tier leaves the digit 3 reproducible only under that scope or at the byte-identical sub-object; that is a register plus disclosure shortfall on a texture claim the row expressly declines to use as a cluster driver, so nothing load-bearing and no byte-false digit. Under the lane test a true cross-row claim phrased in workflow register is low; medium is downgraded to low. The proposed field repair is endorsed with two qualifications: the 3-site sub-object is byte-identical (ketiv plus fully pointed qere), not merely accent-identical, and the 6-verse object should be stated at the skeleton tier with the waw-prefixed oshb:Prov.18.19 named; deleting 'in this part' from all three fields and mirroring every argued site into boundary_evidence_refs is sound. both_sides_assessed false because the item concerns no seam (a count-object and register item); for completeness the row's edges re-derive clean anyway, oshb:Prov.27.14|oshb:Prov.27.15 and oshb:Prov.27.15|oshb:Prov.27.16 each sharing 0 word-bound skeleton tokens, so no span question is open.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways; every digit in the finding re-derives. The definite form is word-bound in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep, word-bound skeleton token האדם, verses: Prov.27.19, Prov.27.20) and the two tokens are byte-identical down to the accents, הָ֝אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Prov.27.19) and הָ֝אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Prov.27.20), byte tier; the bare token אדם (skeleton-tier mention) stands in 33 verses (word-bound, verses) and the contiguous skeleton substring in 44 verses / 46 occurrences, of which oshb:Prov.23.31 is the verb for reddening, not the noun, so the substring object is itself blended and the object must be named before any digit is trusted. The row's three comparanda at the same exact-form tier: זָ֭הָב (oshb:Prov.25.11) is word-bound in 4 verses (Prov.11.22, Prov.20.15, Prov.25.11, Prov.25.12; 7 verses for any prefixed form), הָג֣וֹ (oshb:Prov.25.4) in 2 verses (Prov.25.4, Prov.25.5), עָ֭צֵל (oshb:Prov.26.13) in 12 verses plus וְ֝עָצֵ֗ל (oshb:Prov.26.14) in 1, and all three pairs are byte-identical at their seams exactly as the definite form is here. adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways; both chains are byte-true, with one precision on 'heads'. Vetitive chain: the patach-pointed prohibitive particle (distinct from the segol preposition, which stands once in oshb:Prov.30.10 as אֶל (oshb:Prov.30.10) and is not counted) is word-bound in 64 verses book-wide as the bare token and in 18 more as the waw-prefixed form (sweep, accent-stripped word-bound tokens, verses), and in chapter 30 only at oshb:Prov.30.6, oshb:Prov.30.7, oshb:Prov.30.8 and oshb:Prov.30.10, four of the five verses 30:6-10, as אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ (oshb:Prov.30.6), אַל תִּמְנַ֥ע (oshb:Prov.30.7), אַל תִּֽתֶּן (oshb:Prov.30.8) and אַל תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן (oshb:Prov.30.10), the particle itself byte-identical at all four; it is verse-initial at 30:6 and 30:10 but clause-initial only at 30:7 (after the atnach) and at 30:8, so 'heads' should read clause-initial for those two. Both seams survive, so medium (defective warrant components and undisclosed straddling devices, not alone load-bearing) is confirmed, ruled coherently with the companion item on this row and with the 30:1-6 and 30:10 rows, whose seams are unchanged. The governing rule that decides is the strategy's tier-1 class 'explicit speaker/addressee shifts INSIDE psalms': third-person description of Yahweh's law turns to direct address of Yahweh exactly at the rival seam, and the row's own boundary_rationale concedes the turn ('turns from describing the law's qualities to the psalmist's own response' at web:Ps.19.11). So the rival is not merely mis-rejected on a barred ground; it carries a ruled tier-1 onset warrant the row never weighs, and the rejection is the row's only stated reason for holding the internal boundary decision — that makes the defect load-bearing for that decision: UPGRADE to high under the severity law (load-bearing boundary defect) and under the lane calibration that places a barred evidence class at high where the rival's rejection rests on it. The row's outer edges are untouched by this item and no respan was filed, so span_ruling is n/a; whether the panel is split at web:Ps.19.10|Ps.19.11 or held as one 8-verse strophe under the ~4-8 vv norm is a row-level question for the owner docket, not a book-level one. adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes (shift+1; web:Ps.34.1-Ps.34.3 = oshb:Ps.34.2-Ps.34.4; the seam web:Ps.34.3|Ps.34.4 = oshb:Ps.34.4|Ps.34.5). items.claim: The device_notes plague digit is false and internally inconsistent: the psalm's catalogue represents 8 of the traditional ten plagues, not 7, and 7 covered plus 2 omitted cannot total ten.
items.grounds: device_notes states the sequence '(darkness, blood, frogs, insects, hail, locusts, and the death of the firstborn) covers 7 of the traditional plagues and omits the livestock-pestilence and boils'. From the bytes of 105:28-36 the catalogue names eight distinct plague objects, because 105:31 carries TWO nouns - 'עָרֹ֑ב' and 'כִּ֝נִּ֗ים' - which the sibling row M8-Ps-341 counts separately in its own observed_substrate_signals ('105:31 carries two nouns (arov, kinnim)'); collapsing them into the single word 'insects' is what produces the 7. With exactly two omissions named the arithmetic must close at ten, so 7 is one short on the row's own terms. The count OBJECT is also unnamed and out of scope: 'the traditional plagues' is an Exodus-scoped set that the Ps-scoped staged tools cannot sweep - the section 11 OL-c28 class, where a claim must be scoped explicitly or dropped. The trailing clause 'omits the livestock-pestilence and boils material present in this psalm's own catalogue by their absence' is self-contradictory as written. Not load-bearing: device_notes itself labels the observation 'texture, not boundary authority for these rows', and neither of the row's seams rests on it.

It inherits the row's own claim that the first waw-initial opener at oshb:Ps.105.33 makes oshb:Ps.105.32|oshb:Ps.105.33 'the byte-true rival seam' - but a wayyiqtol is the continuation form, and oshb:Ps.105.33, וַיַּ֣ךְ גַּ֭פְנָם וּתְאֵנָתָ֑ם ... עֵ֣ץ גְּבוּלָֽם, narrates the hail's damage to vines, figs and trees, the consequence line of the plague opened by נָתַ֣ן גִּשְׁמֵיהֶ֣ם בָּרָ֑ד at oshb:Ps.105.32; the same couplet shape recurs at oshb:Ps.105.34-35 (אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א ... then וַיֹּ֣אכַל, the locusts' eating). In this catalogue the ASYNDETIC perfects mark each new plague (105.28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 34) and the wayyiqtols carry consequences (105.33, 105.35) or the climactic strike (105.36): the shipped seam falls between two asyndetic plague openers - as much a list-item boundary as any in 105.28-32 - whereas the 'rival' at 105.32|105.33 would cut one plague from its own consequence line and is byte-WEAKER, not stronger. The formula at 105.31 and 105.34 opens the two swarm plagues, three verses apart with the hail between them: a plague-type formula, not a unit that the seam 'cuts apart'. No ruled device - superscription, hallelu-Yah/hodu frame, doxology, acrostic, explicit speaker/addressee shift, refrain, Selah - stands on either side of any candidate cut. BOTH SIDES of the shipped seam from bytes: oshb:Ps.105.31 closes בְּכָל גְּבוּלָֽם (a totality close; sweep skeleton: 1 verse book-wide) and oshb:Ps.105.32 opens נָתַ֣ן גִּשְׁמֵיהֶ֣ם בָּרָ֑ד (asyndetic perfect, new plague object); the pair's outer seams are likewise content seams - שָֽׂמוּ (oshb:Ps.105.27, third plural, Moses and Aaron) to שָׁ֣לַֽח (oshb:Ps.105.28, third singular, YHWH), and וַיַּ֣ךְ כָּל בְּכ֣וֹר (oshb:Ps.105.36) to וַֽ֭יּוֹצִיאֵם (oshb:Ps.105.37) - so the row's 'content grouping, not a grammatical break' concession is honest and priced at medium, and the finding's part (c) (no tier-1 class at the seam) applies equally to every internal seam of this device-less recital and is cured by none of the proposed cuts. adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes: Psalm 109 is identity-numbered and titled (web:Ps.109.0 is the prefix of oshb:Ps.109.1; 31 WEB = 31 MT verses; the row's dual-cites check via ps_lib). FINDING TESTED AGAINST THE ROW, claim 1: device_notes says the imprecatory register continues into web:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.20 'under different grammar (a motive clause replaces the jussive chain there)'. Bytes: oshb:Ps.109.14 opens יִזָּכֵ֤ר עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו and closes אַל תִּמָּֽח (a jussive-force imperfect and a negative jussive); oshb:Ps.109.15 opens יִהְי֣וּ (jussive force); oshb:Ps.109.19 opens תְּהִי (apocopated jussive); the motive particle יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר stands at oshb:Ps.109.16 alone, its clause continued by the wayyiqtols וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב (oshb:Ps.109.17) and וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ (oshb:Ps.109.18) before תְּהִי resumes the curse and זֹ֤את פְּעֻלַּ֣ת (oshb:Ps.109.20) closes on a verdict label. adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. (1) The tier-4 fact is real and is used as evidence: WEB sets an opening curly quotation mark inside web:Ps.118.15 before its second sentence and the closing mark at the end of web:Ps.118.16; the row's observed_substrate_signals #2 offers that quotation-mark structure as a substrate signal with an absence arm ('the voice of rejoicing (v15a) itself carries no quotation mark'), the driver field labels the unit 'A quoted acclamation', and strongest_rejected_alternative rejects the v16 cut as 'what vv15-16 just quoted as communal acclamation' - translation punctuation doing corroboration work and counterevidence-by-absence, barred by the campaign addendum (E-23). (2) It is corroboration, not the resting point, so medium is the right band: the voice contrast stands in the MT bytes with no punctuation layer - oshb:Ps.118.17 carries three 1cs prefix forms, אָמ֥וּת, אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה, וַ֝אֲסַפֵּ֗ר (byte tier, word indices 1, 3, 4), and oshb:Ps.118.18 two 1cs object suffixes, יִסְּרַ֣נִּי, נְתָנָֽנִי (byte tier), while oshb:Ps.118.15 and oshb:Ps.118.16 carry no first-person form at all; the 'acclamation' reading itself is derivable from oshb:Ps.118.15's own syntax, where ק֤וֹל רִנָּ֬ה וִֽישׁוּעָ֗ה בְּאָהֳלֵ֥י צַדִּיקִ֑ים (byte tier) names a voice and the nominal clause יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל follows as its content. The row's byte claim re-collates: that four-token run stands byte-identically at oshb:Ps.118.15 (word indices 5-8) and oshb:Ps.118.16 (word indices 3-6), and a byte sweep of the run returns exactly those 2 verses. (3) BOTH SIDES of the rival seam at 118:16|118:17 weighed under the book's rules: the preceding unit would close on the doubled clause יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל (second occurrence, oshb:Ps.118.16, byte tier) - a refrain-type close - and the following unit would open לֹֽא אָמ֥וּת (oshb:Ps.118.17, byte tier) on a speaker return to the first person; both are ruled-class signals, so the rival is live on bytes and the row's rejection of it must rest on the byte-grounded voice contrast and on v17 answering vv15-16, never on the quotation marks - which is why the tier-4 lean is a defect and not a stray remark. The row's own edges are sound on ruled classes from both sides: oshb:Ps.118.14 closes in the first person (וַֽיְהִי לִ֝֗י לִֽישׁוּעָֽה, byte tier) and oshb:Ps.118.15 opens on the unaddressed communal scene; oshb:Ps.118.18 closes in the first person (נְתָנָֽנִי) and oshb:Ps.118.19 opens on the 2mp imperative פִּתְחוּ (byte tier), coherent with M8-Ps-395 and M8-Ps-397. (4) Repair validated: the proposed re-grounding on the 1cs distribution is byte-sound and ENDORSED as a field repair (no respan), with two qualifications - name all three v17 forms (the proposal names two) and phrase 'communal' as the row's reading of the voice-clause syntax rather than a byte fact; the WEB quotation mark may remain only as an explicit tier-4 non-evidential disclosure.
