items.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals[3] and device_notes all read: the saints-term (chasidim/chasidav) recurring at 149:1, 149:5, and 149:9 (3 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier). Re-swept at skeleton tier over the MT verse map: the contiguous consonantal substring chet-samekh-yod-dalet occurs in exactly 26 verses -- that is where the digit comes from -- but the two spellings the sentence NAMES, חֲסִידִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.149.5) and חֲסִידָ֗יו (oshb:Ps.149.9), occur in only 10 verses book-wide (2 and 8 respectively). The 16-verse remainder is other forms (MT 4:4, 12:2, 16:10, 18:26, 32:6, 43:1, 50:5, 52:11, 79:2, 86:2, 89:20, 104:17, 132:9, 132:16, 145:10, 145:17), and MT 104:17's member is חֲ֝סִידָ֗ה -- the stork, a different lexeme -- exactly the contained-substring trap the book's sweep hazard catalog names. The load-bearing half of the sentence, 3 of 3 Psalm 149 members, is byte-TRUE and is what keeps the whole_psalm rival live at medium confidence, so the defective digit is not alone load-bearing. The same sentence is carried on the paired row for 149:5-9 (there as 2 of 3 members; 26 verses book-wide), so any cure is a seam-pair cure installed on both.
items.proposed_change: Either rename the object to match the digit (the saints-root chet-samekh-yod-dalet as a consonantal substring: 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier, including the homographic stork at MT 104:17) or keep the named spellings and correct the digit to 10 verses book-wide; install the same wording on the paired 149:5-9 row.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes with the staged Ps tools (sweep.py --skel with --tokens, collate.py, verse_map_oshb.json, pmarks_Ps.json); Ps 149 and Ps 104 are identity psalms in web_mt_offset_map.json, so web:Ps.149.N = oshb:Ps.149.N and web:Ps.104.17 = oshb:Ps.104.17, and the row's refs stand in the right space. (1) COUNT OBJECT. The filed digit reproduces ONLY as the contiguous consonantal substring חסיד at skeleton tier: 26 verses / 26 tokens book-wide. It does not reproduce for the object the sentence names. The two named forms, חֲסִידִֽים (oshb:Ps.149.1, byte tier) and חֲסִידִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.149.5, byte tier) for chasidim and חֲסִידָ֗יו (oshb:Ps.149.9, byte tier) for chasidav, sweep at skeleton tier as חסידים = 2 verses (MT 149:1, 149:5) and חסידיו = 8 verses (MT 30:5, 31:24, 37:28, 85:9, 97:10, 116:15, 148:14, 149:9), 10 verses in all, exactly as the auditor filed. The 16-verse remainder (MT 4:4, 12:2, 16:10, 18:26, 32:6, 43:1, 50:5, 52:11, 79:2, 86:2, 89:20, 104:17, 132:9, 132:16, 145:10, 145:17; re-derived list identical to the finding's) is other inflections of the saints-noun in 15 verses plus, at MT 104:17, חֲ֝סִידָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.104.17, byte tier), the stork, “The stork makes its home in the cypress trees.” (web:Ps.104.17), a different lexeme caught by the contained substring, the very class the toolkit's sweep hazard catalog names as the contained-substring trap. So under the most charitable reading (the saints-noun in every inflection) the honest digit is 25 verses; under the reading the wording invites (the two named forms) it is 10; it is 26 under no reading of the words the saints-term, and the label skeleton tier names a collation level, not a licence to count a broader object than the one named (strategy section 10 count-object discipline: every count names WHAT it counts). Tested against the row: this is not a true claim lacking its digit but a digit bound to the wrong object, so the E-05 lane law yields medium, not low. (2) LOAD-BEARING TEST, seam 149:4|5 weighed from both sides. The preceding unit closes at MT 149:4 כִּֽי רוֹצֶ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה … עֲ֝נָוִ֗ים בִּישׁוּעָֽה (oshb:Ps.149.4, byte tier), a causal grounding clause with no ruled closer: Psalm 149 carries no Selah verse (the word-bound Selah inventory is 71 verses book-wide, none in Psalm 149), no refrain, and no K/Q note (pmarks_Ps.json kq: none in Psalm 149, none at MT 104:17), while the hallelu-Yah frame stands only at the psalm's edges, הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ verse-initial at oshb:Ps.149.1 and הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ verse-final at oshb:Ps.149.9 (byte tier). The following unit opens at MT 149:5 יַעְלְז֣וּ חֲסִידִ֣ים … עַל מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָֽם (oshb:Ps.149.5, byte tier), continuing the yod-preformative jussive chain that runs from יִשְׂמַ֣ח (oshb:Ps.149.2, byte tier) through 149:5; the only mood shifts in the psalm fall at 149:1|2 (the imperative שִׁ֣ירוּ of oshb:Ps.149.1 giving way to jussives) and at 149:6|7 (the infinitive-construct chain לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת oshb:Ps.149.7, לֶאְסֹ֣ר oshb:Ps.149.8, לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת oshb:Ps.149.9, all byte tier). The governing rule that decides is therefore that no tier-1 device stands on either side of 149:4|5: the seam is a discourse turn in setting only, which is exactly the posture the shipped row and its paired row M8-Ps-491 (Ps.149.5-Ps.149.9) both hold at medium with the whole_psalm rival live; the seam pair is coherent and this item does not touch it. The row's 3-of-3 recurrence claim is byte-TRUE (חֲסִידִֽים oshb:Ps.149.1; חֲסִידִ֣ים oshb:Ps.149.5; חֲסִידָ֗יו oshb:Ps.149.9; byte tier) and is what keeps the rival live; the book-wide digit only contextualizes it. Correcting the digit to 25 leaves the argument unchanged, and correcting it to 10 would put 3 of the 10 book-wide verses inside Psalm 149 and make the rival MORE live, not less, so the digit cannot flip the seam and is not load-bearing: medium, not high. It is not low either: the same false digit-object pairing is carried three times in the row (strongest_rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals[3], device_notes) and mirrored on the paired 149:5-9 row (there as 2 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, where the 2-of-3 is likewise byte-true), so any cure is a seam-pair cure. (3) REPAIR PROPOSAL validated from bytes. Option A (rename the object to match 26 and disclose the stork) is byte-sound only if the object is named as the consonantal string חסיד swept as a contained substring, not as the saints-root: 26 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, of which 25 carry the saints-noun and 1 (MT 104:17) the stork. Option B (keep the two named forms and correct the digit to 10 verses book-wide) is byte-sound as re-swept (2 + 8, with all three Psalm 149 members inside those two forms). A third byte-sound wording is the saints-noun in every inflection, 25 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, excluding the homographic stork at MT 104:17 (token-by-token classification of the 26 hits: 7 singular, 2 plural absolute, 16 suffixed, 1 stork). Each remains a PROPOSAL for owner triage, to be installed identically on M8-Ps-490 and M8-Ps-491; span_change is false, so span_ruling is n/a. Verdict: confirm at medium (E-05 count-object overclaim). Same-model-family corroboration of the auditor's re-sweep, not independent confirmation.

items.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative carries no rival boundary at all -- it rejects two unit_type labels -- so this six-verse span ships without engagement of any rival cut, including one its own prose points at.
items.grounds: The field rejects forcing the span into wasf_poem or narrative_sequence as a worse fit than lyric_address, and says the span is argued into lyric_address by the closest-fit operative category with the deviation disclosed below. That is a unit_type justification, and the book's operative-category law routes exactly that disclosure to device_notes, where this row already carries it -- so the rival-boundary slot is spent on a duplicate. A rival cut was available from the row's own bytes: MT 3:7-3:10 carry no first- or second-person address form at all (verified -- every suffix across those four verses is third-person), and MT 3:11 then opens צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte), two 2fp imperatives plus the book's only daughters-of-Zion vocative (sweep: 1 verse), which under the book's voice policy is tier-1 voice-shift evidence standing exactly at the 3:10|3:11 junction. The row's own device_notes concedes the point by saying the addressee shift to the daughters of Zion only surfaces at the closing imperative in Song.3.11, and separately discloses a span-internal setumah at MT 3:8 (single-witness tier-3, correctly non-driving) at the other candidate joint. I am NOT concluding that the shipped span is wrong -- the maximal-run rule and the processional coherence support holding MT 3:6-3:11 whole -- only that the strongest available rival is unengaged, which is a warrant gap on a medium_low row. Noted inside the same sentence and folded into this finding rather than scored separately: the phrase closest-fit operative category imports governance vocabulary into row prose.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the unit_type sentence with an actual rival-cut engagement -- reject, or accept and re-span, the 3:10|3:11 cut at the daughters-of-Zion vocative onset, quoting the pointed splice at oshb:Song.3.11 with its tier -- and leave the operative-category deviation disclosure where it already stands in device_notes. Any resulting respan is an adjudication question, not this review's proposal.

adjudication.grounds: CONFIRM at medium (rival-engagement: a defective warrant at an internal tier-1 joint, not alone load-bearing). Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. (1) The finding's factual ground holds. Every suffix and verb form across oshb:Song.3.6-Song.3.10 is third person: 3fs עֹלָה֙ and מְקֻטֶּ֤רֶת (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier); 3ms/3fs מִטָּתוֹ֙ ... לָ֑הּ (oshb:Song.3.7, byte tier); 3mp/3ms כֻּלָּם֙ ... חַרְבּוֹ֙ עַל יְרֵכ֔וֹ (oshb:Song.3.8, byte tier); עָ֤שָׂה לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.9, byte tier); עַמּוּדָיו֙ ... רְפִידָת֣וֹ ... מֶרְכָּב֖וֹ ... תּוֹכוֹ֙ (oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier). A scan of the pointed bytes of those five verses finds no final-kaf suffix (the only final-kaf tokens are the noun הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ at MT 3:9 and בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ at MT 3:11), no 1cs -ti perfect, no 1cp -nu form and no independent first- or second-person pronoun; the yod-final tokens are construct plurals (form claims argued from the pointed bytes plus the WEB rendering; no morphology layer is staged). Then oshb:Song.3.11 opens צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (byte tier; WEB “Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see” web:Song.3.11): two feminine-plural imperatives plus the daughters-of-Zion vocative, which the book's voice policy lists by name among its tier-1 formula anchors (adjacent-pair sweep, skeleton tier: 1 verse, MT 3:11; the daughters-of-Jerusalem pair sweeps 7 verses at skeleton tier only because it catches the from-phrase מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם at oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier, which is not an address). So a tier-1-marked rival cut stands at the 3:10|3:11 joint exactly as the finding says. (2) BOTH SIDES of that rival seam weighed from bytes. The preceding verse closes תּוֹכוֹ֙ רָצ֣וּף אַהֲבָ֔ה מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier) with no parashah seg at MT 3:10 (the WLC inventory's segs in this span sit at MT 3:8 and MT 3:11, single-witness, tier-3; absence is never counterevidence). The following verse continues the same referent after its summons: בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ... לּ֤וֹ אִמּוֹ֙ ... וּבְי֖וֹם שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier) carries on the 3ms suffix chain of MT 3:9-3:10 and the Shelomo chain שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.7, byte tier) / שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.9, byte tier) / שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier) (Shelomo-skeleton sweep: 8 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, one of them the homograph at MT 1:7; 3 of the 8 inside this span). The governing rule that decides: the hybrid granularity permits a cut at a tier-1 marker but does not compel one, and the summons-to-view reads as the unit's own close because its object is the king the description has been building (tier-2 referential continuity, used here only to reject a cut, never to drive a seam), corroborated at tier 3 by the setumah standing AT MT 3:11 rather than at MT 3:10 (single witness). The shipped span is therefore defensible and I propose no respan. (3) The shipped row's defect is real. Its strongest_rejected_alternative rejects two unit_type labels (wasf_poem, narrative_sequence) and names no rival cut; the operative-category law routes exactly that deviation disclosure to device_notes, where the row already carries it, so the rival slot is spent on a duplicate. The row's only engagement of the 3:10|3:11 joint is the device_notes concession that the addressee shift surfaces at the closing imperative, while boundary_rationale treats a marker of the book's own tier-1 class as a unit-internal close without saying why it does not open a unit. That is an unargued warrant at the one internal joint where the book's law demands engagement: a defective warrant, medium. Not high, because both outer seams stand on tier-1 anchors weighed from both sides: front, the full adjuration הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Song.3.5, byte tier; setumah at MT 3:5, single-witness tier-3) closes the seek-find episode and מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier; collates byte against oshb:Song.8.5 as well; ascent-formula sweep, skeleton tier: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5; bare mi-zot interrogative 3 verses, MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5) opens a fresh 3fs question; rear, MT 3:11 closes on שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier; setumah at MT 3:11, single-witness tier-3) and הִנָּ֨ךְ יָפָ֤ה רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.4.1, byte tier) opens the his-word address, coherent with the adjacent shipped rows Song.3.5-Song.3.5 and Song.4.1-Song.4.7, which argue those same seams from their own sides. Not low: this is not a mechanical or register slip but the missing half of the row's own warrant for a six-verse span (the register bleed the auditor folded in, the governance phrase closest-fit operative category inside row prose, is a genuine low-severity component and moves the severity neither way). (4) Repair proposal tested as adversarially as the row: the field repair is byte-sound and is ENDORSED AS A PROPOSAL for owner triage, with this qualification: the replacement sentence should REJECT the 3:10|3:11 cut on the grounds in (2) (the 3ms referential chain and the Shelomo chain binding MT 3:11 to MT 3:9-3:10; the setumah at MT 3:11 disclosed single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only), quoting the pointed onset splice of oshb:Song.3.11 with its byte tier, and leave the deviation disclosure in device_notes; the accept-and-respan branch is not supported by these bytes and is not proposed. Non-span item: span_change false, span_ruling n/a; both sides of every seam in play were weighed from bytes.

adjudication.grounds: CONFIRM at medium (E-05 count-object blend: a false digit at the object named, not load-bearing). Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. (1) The row's parenthetical names the pointed token הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) as a byte-sweep object and attaches two digits, 1 verse book-wide and 2 occurrences in-verse.
